VIEW-002.was: An operator can save a named combination of filters, sort, grouping, and list or board layout as private or shared, then update, duplicate, or delete it. A private view is visible and editable only by its owner; anyone who can see a shared view's teams can open or duplicate it (a Guest only when it covers only their invited teams), but only its owner can update or delete it, and ownership changes only under OPS-004. Deleting a view never changes an issue.

NOTIFY-001.summary: Inbox events: clause text revised for the full-product target contract (published clause, status partial).
NOTIFY-001.was: Vector creates an in-app notification, visible within 5 seconds, for assignment of an issue to the operator, a direct mention (ISSUE-013), a comment on an issue they follow, the return of an intake item they deferred, the resolution of the last blocker on an issue assigned to them, and a due reminder (NOTIFY-005). Assignment and direct-mention events may also send the minimal transactional email defined by NOTIFY-006; all other product notification events remain in-app.
NOTIFY-001.now: Vector creates an in-app notification, visible within 5 seconds, for assignment of an issue to the member, a direct mention (ISSUE-013), a comment on an issue they follow, the return of an intake item they deferred, the resolution of the last blocker on an issue assigned to them, a due reminder (NOTIFY-005), a triage item they are responsible for (TRIAGE-001), a project or initiative update they follow (PROJ-010), a delegated agent's question or completion (AGENT-002), a review request or status change from Git (GITHUB-005) and an SLA warning (AUTO-004). Members who follow an issue (NOTIFY-002) — its creator, assignee, commenters, mentioned members and explicit followers — are also notified when it is completed, when it is canceled or marked duplicate, when its status changes to another status (one notification per change, grouped with any other change made in the same mutation), when its priority is raised to Urgent, when it becomes blocked by a newly added blocker or a blocking relation on it is added or removed, when its due date changes, and when a resolved thread they took part in is reopened (ISSUE-008). Each event notifies each follower once, never the actor (NOTIFY-003), and a completion caused by automation or Git (GITHUB-003) names that automation as actor. The inbox is always delivered; email, Slack, Teams, mobile push and desktop follow NOTIFY-006 and NOTIFY-007.

Base delivery attempts, backoff, cooldown and accepted/rejected/uncertain results survive restart. Ambiguous sends never retry under fresh IDs; explicit reconciliation requires receiver evidence. WEBHOOK-001.now: Registered public HTTPS destinations receive minimal native created/updated/completed issue events under stable business identities. Base delivery attempts, backoff, cooldown and accepted/rejected/uncertain results survive restart. Ambiguous sends never retry under fresh IDs; explicit reconciliation requires receiver evidence. Mapped imports and restore create no delivery events. DATA-011.summary: Erasing an imported person: clause text revised for the full-product target contract (published clause, status partial).
DATA-011.was: An operator can erase a person that imports carried, by exact email and/or up to five exact display names, after a counts-only preview and a typed confirmation. One D1 batch removes the person from every import run, applied or still pending: records that hold them become permanent tombstones that never publish or replay, runs labelled with their email are retired, originals holding them are withdrawn, imported comments they wrote read as deleted with no author name, reconciliation reports lose those cells, and development mail naming them is dropped. Issues already written stay; a pending run still finishes, without the erased records and without links to them. A current member or invitation is refused until OPS-004 removal. The erasure journal is append-only, and an archive made before the erasure is refused on restore when a later archive's journal is supplied.
DATA-011.now: An Owner or Admin (role matrix; Members and Guests are refused 403) can erase a person that imports carried, by exact email and/or up to five exact display names, after a counts-only preview and a typed confirmation. One D1 batch removes the person from every import run, applied or still pending: records that hold them become permanent tombstones that never publish or replay, runs labelled with their email are retired, originals holding them are withdrawn, imported comments they wrote read as deleted with no author name, reconciliation reports lose those cells, and development mail naming them is dropped. Issues already written stay; a pending run still finishes, without the erased records and without links to them. A current or suspended member, or an open invitation, is refused here; a member's native and imported records are erased together by ROLE-012. The erasure journal is append-only, and an archive made before the erasure is refused on restore when a later archive's journal is supplied.

agentUpdateInstructions: Upgrade from 0.2.0 by merging this release into your checkout, keeping your customisations and every applied migration byte. Back up first: stop rer dev and run rer export --output exports/vector.jsonl; for a hosted installation, run node node_modules/@runeditrun/rer/modules/portability/cli.mjs export --origin ORIGIN --session-file PRIVATE_FILE --out ABSOLUTE_ARCHIVE with the owner's one __Host-operator_session cookie in a mode-600 file (rer export refuses a hosted origin and wrangler d1 export refuses Vector's FTS5 tables). Run rer install with the pinned @runeditrun/rer 0.2.62, then rer dev (local) or git pull --ff-only and rer deploy (hosted); both apply the fifteen additive migrations 0050 to 0064 in order after unchanged 0001-0049. Migration 0053 rebuilds notification_candidates and notification_type_mutes by copy; retain them and every later table on compatible-source rollback. The independent 0.3.0 gate upgraded a populated 0.2.0 local install (49 to 64 migrations) with its intake decision, comment and file bytes intact. Hosted HTTP restore into an rer-deployed installation is refused with restore_bootstrap_not_pristine because rer's owner claim leaves a second session; restore a hosted archive locally with rer import. Development has no captured-mail inbox; local sign-in uses rer dev's RER_OPEN owner entry. seed.json's description is the one plain catalogue sentence. Do not broaden claims: Linear and Jira importers remain synthetic-only, there is no Asana importer, and Managed relay delivery, hosted Cron timing and capacity are not proven.
publicReleaseNotes:
Vector 0.3.0 is the planning and follow-up release. Issues gain structured descriptions with checklists and a description history, comment threads you can resolve, follower notifications, snoozes and personal reminders, and ten-second Undo. Planning gains ordered sub-issues with automatic parent progress, related issues, issue copies from the menu, the command palette or the API, a shared manual order, per-person workload, project start dates, priorities, labels and a stated reason for project health, and automatic team cycle schedules.

Reports from monitoring or support tools reach Needs decision through a secret webhook URL (with Zapier, Make and UptimeRobot steps) as well as signed senders. Moving in now also accepts Plane CSV, Shortcut CSV and Huly JSON files through the same reviewed, staged import.

Checked before release: an independent gate ran Vector's whole loop locally at 1440 and 390 and on a hosted installation with real email: a source report landed in Needs decision, was deferred and came back on time (and sooner when new evidence arrived), was accepted with a reason and routed into Now; Current, My work, Board, saved views, Inbox, project health, cycle rollover and Command-K search all worked; an invited teammate signed in from the emailed link and received assignment email, and the owner received mention email. A populated v0.2.0 installation upgraded with its data (migrations 0050 to 0064). A hosted backup was taken, the installation removed and redeployed, and the backup restored with all its records and file bytes.

Known issues: restoring a backup into a hosted installation made by rer deploy is refused (restore_bootstrap_not_pristine), so restore locally with rer import; a hosted backup uses Base's transfer client with the owner's session (see CHANGELOG.md), because rer export and wrangler d1 export cannot read the hosted database. The deferral return time is entered in your browser's time zone.
